fact: BUNEC director-general Alexandre Marie Yomo said on 14 September 2026 that the digitisation pilot begun in 2020 has digitised 60 of Cameroon's 432 civil-registration centres (13.9%), up from 42 in April 2022, with full completeness targeted for 2029-2030 if funded.

UNDP says the Système Intégré de Gestion de l'État Civil (SIGEC), with the SANEC digital archive, is being rolled out under its Legal Identity II project with BUNEC in six East Region communes including Bertoua, Batouri and Abong-Mbang, with Bertoua 1er already in production producing birth and marriage acts.

Cameroon's human rights commission (CDHC) said on 10 August 2026 that BUNEC's national civil-registry modernisation plan 2025-2029 was launched on 11 September 2025 and urged the government to fund BUNEC and communes to complete the digital coverage of the national civil registry file.

MINDDEVEL's deck says law 2024/016 consecrates digitalisation of civil-event registration, creates the national civil-status file, and validates electronic civil-status acts produced in pilot operations.

UNDP says it supported digitalisation of civil registration in 18 communes of the Far North, North-West and South-West, and on 5 June 2026 deployed the SIGEC civil-status system at Bertoua city hall, producing the East Region's first digitised birth certificate, with seven East communes covered by the project.
